@graph.name: ClinVar VCV XML
@graph.description: The Cascade Bridge Adapter for ClinVar VCV XML: the package of data a Cascade Bridge runs to turn NCBI ClinVar variation records into Cascade RDF, the pilot adapter. Import-only. This crate is the adapter's manifest: a Bridge reads the root entity first, for the format id (identifier, the same string cascade-cli accepts for --from, from src/lib/clinvar-converter/registry-entry.ts), the source schema, the two envelopes, the unit, the detect rule, the profile the Bridge must offer, the vocabulary pin, the gap scheme every finding takes its body from, each gap declaring the sh:resultSeverity its findings carry where that is not sh:Info, the accounting of every path its source carries, whose entry reports the gap it names and the test manifest; the data entities carry provenance for every committed fixture, schema and document and for every remote dataset the adapter references. Committed inputs carry a sha256 computed locally over the committed bytes. Remote datasets carry the md5 NCBI publishes in the .md5 file beside each release. Four inputs and their expected graphs are taken from the conformance repository, the inputs byte for byte and the expected graphs corrected where the converter that produced them was wrong; their fetch date and method were not recorded when they were captured, and each entry says so. The four expected findings are the output of a Bridge's convert --findings over the committed input beside them. Dates and sizes for remote files were read from ftp.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov on 2026-09-06. Its three lookup tables are SKOS concept maps under vocab/, each declared as a bridge:table and read by the mapping queries that look a value up in it; this adapter's own namespace carries its gaps and nothing else, so no value yet needs a bridge:extensionVocabulary. Nothing for the export direction is declared, because ClinVar is import-only.

@graph.name: efetch
@graph.description: E-utilities efetch (db=clinvar, rettype=vcv). All five committed inputs. NCBI's XSD does not declare this root; the wrapper schema named as the document schema adds it, so a whole efetch response validates.

@graph.name: release
@graph.description: The monthly and weekly release files, ClinVarVCVRelease_*.xml.gz. Declared by NCBI's XSD directly, so no document schema beyond the source schema is needed. The root element is still ClinVarVariationRelease although the file name family changed to ClinVarVCVRelease in August 2025; docs/format.md, "The two envelopes".

@graph.name: sparql-1.1
@graph.description: Declared in the Cascade Bridge Specification's vocabulary, vocab/bridge.ttl in cascade-bridge-spec.

@graph.name: Cascade Bridge Adapter profile
@graph.description: The RO-Crate 1.2 Profile Crate a conforming adapter package names in conformsTo: the machine-checkable claim that this crate is an adapter package, whose constraints resource is the SHACL shapes in cascade-bridge-spec. The IRI does not dereference yet, which that repository's README records; the Profile Crate describing it is adapter/profile/ro-crate-metadata.json there.

@graph.name: spec at d819bc2
@graph.description: The spec revision the adapter's vocabularies are pinned to: the-cascade-protocol/spec at the merge commit of its PR #56 (2026-09-08), which the tag vocab/core-v3.9 points at and keeps reachable. Every genomics: and core: term the expected graphs write has the same standing here as at jayostis/spec e77ba5e, the fork revision conformance/scripts/SPEC_PIN names: the fork's later releases add nothing this adapter writes. One term is declared at neither: cascade:sourceFhirId, which every record carries. Read on 2026-09-13. A web-based data entity, referenced and not committed, the way the release files are: the RO-Crate 1.2 validator reads every SoftwareSourceCode as a script that must be a File in hasPart.

@graph.name: Cascade genomics vocabulary
@graph.description: One of the two Cascade vocabularies the adapter writes. Pre-stable: at the pin, ontologies/genomics/v1-draft/genomics.ttl carries owl:versionInfo "1.0-draft.0.5"; the version recorded here is the draft label. Its terms go through spec's own process; none is minted in this adapter.

@graph.name: Cascade core vocabulary
@graph.description: One of the two Cascade vocabularies the adapter writes. At the pin, ontologies/core/v1/core.ttl carries owl:versionInfo "3.9", the version spec's VOCAB_VERSIONS records. The stamp predicates the test manifest ignores when comparing (cascade:dataProvenance, cascade:schemaVersion) are its terms.

@graph.name: ClinVar VCV XSD, version 2.6, pinned copy
@graph.description: NCBI's schema pinned byte for byte: the source schema every VariationArchive unit is validated against, and the schema schema/ClinVarResult-Set.xsd includes. Identical to the file at the isBasedOn URL, whose entity carries NCBI's date and the note on 2.5: md5 is NCBI's sibling .md5 file, sha256 is computed locally over the committed bytes. Never edited; to change it, replace it from its source and update contentSize, sha256 and md5 in the same commit. docs/format.md says why 2.6 and not 2.5 is pinned.

@graph.name: efetch envelope wrapper schema
@graph.description: Includes NCBI's ClinVar_VCV_2.6.xsd unchanged and declares the one document root NCBI's schema leaves undeclared, ClinVarResult-Set, so a whole efetch response validates and not only the records inside it. The document schema of the efetch envelope (#envelope-efetch); .vscode/settings.json associates fixtures/in/*.xml with it.

@graph.name: Detect rule
@graph.description: The detect rule, bridge:detectQuery: an ASK over the envelope skeleton, true for an efetch envelope holding records or the empty set efetch returns when a query matched none, and for a release envelope holding records.

@graph.name: Mapping: the Variant
@graph.description: One genomics:Variant per VariationArchive, named by a UUID the query mints from the VCV accession, so the other two record classes can point at it without a lookup.

@graph.name: Mapping: the interpretations
@graph.description: One genomics:VariantInterpretation per condition of each RCV whose classification is one of the five ACMG classes, and its genomics:aggregatedFrom links to the submitter assertions whose TraitMapping names that condition. The links are written here because their subject and their keys are the interpretation's.

@graph.name: Mapping: the submitter assertions
@graph.description: One genomics:SubmitterAssertion per ClinicalAssertion with an SCV accession and a germline classification among the five ACMG classes.

@graph.name: Findings: the Variant
@graph.description: What the Variant record carries that has no Cascade term, as Web Annotations on the SimpleAllele, the aggregate Classifications block and the TraitMappingList.

@graph.name: Findings: the interpretations
@graph.description: Web Annotations on each RCVAccession and the conditions under it, including why an RCV yields no interpretation.

@graph.name: Findings: the submitter assertions
@graph.description: Web Annotations on each ClinicalAssertion and what hangs off it, including why an assertion yields no record.

@graph.name: ClinVar VCV gaps
@graph.description: The scheme every finding this adapter reports takes its body from: one skos:Concept per gap, in this adapter's own namespace (https://ns.cascadeprotocol.org/adapter/clinvar/v1-draft#), each under one of the five bridge:gapKinds the Cascade Bridge Specification declares and naming at most one Cascade term that would close it.

@graph.name: ClinVar VCV source accounting
@graph.description: What this adapter does with each path of its source: one bridge:PathEntry per distinct element and attribute path of the four judged inputs, 412 of them, each with exactly one of the six bridge:verdicts and whatever that verdict names. Four of them also declare a lookup: the concept map under vocab/ that their path's values are looked up in, and the gap a value that map holds no notation for opens. A path is written from the record element, VariationArchive, so it is the same under both envelopes; the record element's own path carries no entry and its attributes do. The paths were enumerated with lxml over fixtures/in/'s four judged inputs on 2026-09-20. Each verdict is a claim read against in/sparql/, and not one the lint can settle: the lint tests only that a path claiming carriage has its last step named somewhere in a mapping file. Paths that only clinvar-vcv-release-2026-09 or fixtures/in/VCV_XML_VCV000091629.xml carry are not in it.

@graph.name: ClinVar germline classification values
@graph.description: The concept map in/sparql/assertion.rq and in/sparql/interpretation.rq look a germline classification up in: one skos:Concept per ClinVar classification phrase, its skos:notation the phrase lowercased and trimmed of XML whitespace, its skos:exactMatch the Cascade term. The five ACMG/AMP terms are the ones this adapter carries; the isBasedOn page, Representation of classifications in ClinVar, read on 2026-09-21, names them and also lists the values ClinVar accepts beyond them, which this map deliberately does not carry, so each of those is reported as a gap.

@graph.name: ClinVar review statuses
@graph.description: The concept map in/sparql/interpretation.rq looks an RCV's review status up in: one skos:Concept per ClinVar review status phrase, its skos:notation the phrase lowercased and trimmed of XML whitespace, its skos:exactMatch the Cascade term. The isBasedOn page, Review status in ClinVar, read on 2026-09-21, publishes the statuses and their star ratings; it lists the current spellings, and this map also carries the earlier spellings of the conflicting tier that the committed records still hold.

@graph.name: ClinVar submitting organization categories
@graph.description: The concept map in/sparql/assertion.rq looks a ClinVarAccession/@OrganizationCategory up in: one skos:Concept per category phrase, its skos:notation the phrase lowercased and trimmed of XML whitespace, its match the Cascade term, skos:closeMatch where the phrase and the term do not mean the same thing. ClinVar's schema types the attribute xs:string and publishes no page of its values, so two sources stand behind these rows and neither is enough alone, both read on 2026-09-21. organization_summary.txt's institution type column is the published listing of what the data carries - lab, clinic, other, consortium, LSDB, patient registry, resource and access - which spells two of this map's phrases in shorter form and names none of the panel, research-group and clinician ones. Submission Overview names those as prose under Can I submit to ClinVar?: clinical testing labs, research labs, genetics clinics, patient registries, locus-specific databases, expert panels, groups establishing practice guidelines.

@graph.name: Test manifest
@graph.description: The cases a Bridge's harness executes and how each is judged: a W3C-style test manifest (mf: test-manifest vocabulary) whose entries are typed with the bridge: vocabulary and constrained by the SHACL shapes, both of them in the Cascade Bridge Specification (vocab/bridge.ttl and shapes/bridge.shapes.ttl in cascade-bridge-spec). This adapter carried copies of the two until 0.2.0; they were the seed of that repository, and a second statement of a contract is one that can disagree with it. Every input, expected graph, findings file, dataset and envelope this manifest names is described in this crate, by the same IRI, and it names this crate's root entity as its adapter, so the manifest and this crate load as one graph.

@graph.name: Expected graph for VCV000007105
@graph.description: The Cascade RDF the input produces through cascade-cli's ClinVar converter, as committed to the conformance repository at 8a5e203 (2026-05-06) and taken from 0ea48bb, with one correction. The converter paired each condition of RCV002490332 with the TraitSet's Trait at the same position, and ClinVar lists the two in different orders, so four interpretations carried another condition's MONDO. Here each condition takes the MONDO of the Trait carrying its MedGen ID: four condition and mondoId values move to their own interpretations, and the 62 aggregatedFrom links the misaligned Traits produced are removed. 1,424 triples, 112 IRI subjects named urn:uuid: by the converter.

@graph.name: ClinVar VCV monthly release, 2026-09
@graph.description: Every VariationArchive in ClinVar at ReleaseDate 2026-08-29, in the ClinVarVariationRelease envelope (#envelope-release), declaring xsi:noNamespaceSchemaLocation http://ftp.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pub/clinvar/xsd_public/ClinVar_VCV_2.6.xsd (read from the first 256 KB of the file on 2026-09-06). md5 is NCBI's, from the sibling .md5 file. Size and date are from the HTTPS headers (Last-Modified 2026-09-03T04:07:26Z). Referenced by its dated name; ClinVarVCVRelease_00-latest.xml.gz is a symlink to it and is never the reference. Monthly releases are generated on the first Thursday of the month. Not committed. No weekly release is listed: on 2026-09-06 the weekly symlink under weekly_release/ resolved to this file, and a Dataset entity with no content of its own is not something a Bridge can run; a dated weekly is added here, with its contentUrl, md5, contentSize, version and datePublished, when one exists (docs/format.md, "Releases").

@graph.name: ClinVar VCV XSD, version 2.6
@graph.description: NCBI's published schema, pinned byte for byte as schema/ClinVar_VCV_2.6.xsd. Its version attribute reads "2.6; February 26, 2026"; dateModified is the HTTPS Last-Modified. md5 is NCBI's sibling .md5 file, checked against the download; sha256 is computed locally. ClinVar_VCV.xsd and ClinVar_VCV_weekly.xsd on the same site publish the same md5. It supersedes 2.5 (md5 169e958e2f06c6a3ba8a96aae3a949a9, "2.5; August 6, 2025"); the whole difference is one optional derived_by attribute, enumerated to NCBI, on SetElementSetType. The 2026-09 monthly release declares 2.6, which is why 2.6 and not 2.5 is pinned.

@graph.name: conformance fixtures/genomics/clinvar at 0ea48bb
@graph.description: The four input / expected pairs the committed oracles are taken from; the inputs are unchanged and four expected graphs are corrected in this crate. The gaps sidecars beside them are the source of nothing here: the findings oracles are a Bridge's own convert --findings output. A contextual entity: the source of the fixtures, not part of the crate. The commit is on the fork, jayostis/conformance, and is not an ancestor of the-cascade-protocol/conformance main, so this entity and the oracles' links name the fork: naming the org would point at a revision the org does not hold. The directory last changed at 8a5e203 (2026-05-06, "feat(conformance): clinvar VCV expected.ttl + gaps.json oracles for 4 VCVs"), which is on the org's main with identical blobs; the same bytes are readable from the org at that commit. The conformance suite validates the expected graphs against the spec revision in its scripts/SPEC_PIN, jayostis/spec at e77ba5e; this adapter pins the-cascade-protocol/spec instead (bridge:cascadeVocabularyPin).
